reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Ten-resident petition form requesting state veterinary surgeon
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including the statutory petition table form) and source history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14193, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070; prior revisions 1929–1909). Covers ten state residents appearing before a clerk of a court of record or associate circuit judge to demand the state veterinary surgeon's services using the prescribed petition form addressed to the director of agriculture.

headings.title: Optional official certification form for resident petition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including the statutory certification table form) and source notes. Uses permissive language ('may be certified') for a court clerk or associate circuit judge to certify that the petitioners are known reputable county citizens.

headings.title: Health department requests for veterinary disease and food inspection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Authorizes the Department of Health and Senior Services, through its director, to demand the state veterinary surgeon's services from the director of agriculture for human-transmissible diseases and examination of meats, milk, and foods when deemed necessary by the department. Independent review revised title to cover both human-transmissible disease inspection and examination of meats, milk, and foods.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections, both embedded statutory form tables in subsections 1 and 2, and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14193, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070; 1929–1909); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked ten-resident threshold, permissive certification ("may be certified"), and DHSS demand scope. Retained subsections 1–2 and revised subsection 3 to cover both human-transmissible disease inspection and meat, milk, and food examination.

headings.title: Diagnostic laboratories, fee schedule, and eradication-program exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 H.B. 878 §§ 66, 67, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52, A.L. 1995 S.B. 3, A.L. 1996 S.B. 766). Covers establishment of the Animal Health Diagnostic Laboratories under the state veterinarian, fee assessment authority fixed by rule of the director of agriculture, and the fee exemption for diagnostic tests under state-federal cooperative eradication programs.

headings.title: Animal Health Laboratory Fee Fund creation and purpose
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers depositing collected laboratory fees via the Department of Revenue into the newly created Animal Health Laboratory Fee Fund for laboratory use and specifies the fund does not substitute for already appropriated general revenue bonds.

headings.title: Biennial non-lapse, fee adjustments, and general revenue transfers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Preserves the express 'notwithstanding section 33.080' biennial non-lapse rule, mandatory fee-schedule adjustment when the biennial balance exceeds $200,000 to stay at or below $225,000, and transfer of any fiscal-year-end excess above $225,000 to general revenue.

headings.title: Investment of surplus fund balances and accrued income
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs the state treasurer to invest unneeded Animal Health Laboratory Fee Fund sums in interest-bearing accounts or U.S. government obligations as provided by law, with all investment income accruing back to the fund.

headings.title: Chapter 267 rulemaking compliance with section 536.024
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Conditions effectiveness of any rule or portion of a rule promulgated under chapter 267 on promulgation pursuant to section 536.024. Independent review revised title to make the chapter-wide scope ("authority of this chapter") explicit.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections and history notes (L. 1992 H.B. 878 §§ 66, 67 through A.L. 1996 S.B. 766); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked eradication-program fee exemption, non-substitution for appropriated general revenue bonds, section 33.080 non-lapse, $200,000/$225,000 thresholds, and chapter-wide section 536.024 rulemaking condition. Retained subsections 1–4 and revised subsection 5 to state chapter 267 scope.

headings.title: Voluntary identification and limits on mandatory NAIS registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 931). Covers permissive state support for a voluntary animal identification program and bars the Department of Agriculture from mandating national animal identification system (NAIS) premises registration without specific statutory authorization from the General Assembly.

headings.title: Participant withdrawal, data deletion, and disease-program exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers a NAIS participant's right to withdraw at any time and deletion of personal information upon withdrawal, expressly qualified by the exception for ongoing disease investigations or disease monitoring or control programs.

headings.title: Gubernatorial waiver for livestock marketing and expiration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers the governor's conditional executive-order authority to waive section 267.168 in whole or part if it interferes with Missouri livestock marketing, with automatic expiration at the end of the next regular or governor-called special legislative session. Independent review revised title to include the automatic expiration of the executive order after the next regular or special session.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 2008 S.B. 931); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked permissive voluntary-program support, legislative-authorization qualifier on mandatory NAIS premises registration, disease-program exception to data deletion, and session-end expiration of the governor's waiver. Retained subsections 1–2 and revised subsection 3 to capture waiver expiration.

headings.title: Definition of animal referencing section 277.020
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 2016 H.B. 1414; vetoed July 8, 2016, overridden September 14, 2016, effective 10-14-16 per § 21.250). Defines 'animal' for section 267.169 by exact cross-reference to 'livestock' in section 277.020.

headings.title: Traceability data exempt from chapter 610 public disclosure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1)–(3)) and veto-override effective-date note. Excludes premises registration, animal identification, and animal tracking data collected under the federal Animal Disease Traceability Program or any successor program from public-record status and chapter 610 disclosure.

headings.title: Required release for disease outbreaks and public safety
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 (including subdivisions (1)–(3)) and source notes. Qualified by 'notwithstanding subsection 2' and 'to the extent that', requiring a state agency director or the state veterinarian to release otherwise closed data when useful to control or prevent a disease outbreak, for public safety, or to show whether particular animals or herds are involved in an outbreak.

headings.title: Permitted aggregate, consented, and regulatory-compliance disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 (including subdivisions (1)–(3)) and source notes. Clarifies that section 267.169 does not bar disclosing non-identifying statistical or aggregate data, data disclosed with a farmer's or rancher's expressed written consent, or information required by law for state agency regulatory compliance.

headings.title: Knowing-release violations, civil actions, damages, and attorney fees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Establishes that knowingly releasing protected data violates the section, authorizes any person or entity alleging a violation to sue in a court of competent jurisdiction, and allows discretionary appropriate relief including up to $10,000 in damages and reasonable attorney's fees.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections, all subdivisions in subsections 2–4, and the 2016 veto-override and effective-date notes (L. 2016 H.B. 1414; vetoed July 8, 2016; overridden September 14, 2016; effective 10-14-16 per § 21.250); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked exact section 277.020 and chapter 610 cross-references, mandatory qualified outbreak/public-safety releases vs. permissive disclosures, and knowing-release remedies. Retained all five headings as accurate and neutral.

headings.title: Discretionary tuberculosis indemnity for approved herd control programs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 14200, A. 1949 S.B. 1094, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1816; prior revisions 1929, 1919; effective 5-10-78). Preserves permissive payment authority ('may pay'), appropriation limits, and eligibility tied to owners conducting an approved tuberculosis control program for exposed, infected, or reactor cattle.

headings.title: Valuation criteria and three-copy appraisement forms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Covers the valuation cap recognized by the state veterinarian and owner as just compensation based on market conditions, breeding value, and other criteria, separate animal identification, and three-copy distribution of appraisement forms.

headings.title: Isolation, slaughter sale deadline, and loss calculation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Requires isolating indemnity-claimed cattle, selling them for slaughter within 15 days of identification or branding, reporting net slaughter proceeds after expenses to the department, and computing owner loss as appraised value minus net proceeds.

headings.title: Indemnity cap, state certification, and warrant payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Covers the state veterinarian setting the indemnity not exceeding breeding value, department certification to the commissioner of administration as a legal claim within available appropriations, and warrant payment on the state treasurer.

headings.title: Owner cooperation condition and ineligibility bars
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Conditions reactor or infected-cattle indemnity on owner cooperation in recommended eradication practices and bars payment if the state veterinarian determines the animal does not qualify or the owner is ineligible.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 14200, A. 1949 S.B. 1094, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1816; prior revisions 1929, 1919; effective 5-10-78); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked permissive appropriation-limited payment, valuation and three-copy appraisement rules, 15-day slaughter sale and net-proceeds deduction, breeding-value cap, and cooperation/ineligibility conditions. Retained all five headings.

headings.title: Class A misdemeanor for obstruction or quarantine violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14217, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1816, A.L. 1983 1st Ex. Sess. H.B. 11, A.L. 1987 H.B. 368; prior revisions 1929–1909). Covers obstructing the state veterinarian, violating sections 267.010 to 267.730 or official quarantine orders after notice, and violating district or municipality quarantine provisions.

headings.title: Authorization of department and USDA enforcement employees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Grants the department director authority to designate department or USDA employees to assist in enforcing sections 267.010 to 267.730.

headings.title: Livestock vehicle stops and red flashing light authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Permits authorized enforcement employees to intercept, stop, and detain vehicles carrying livestock in Missouri for official inspection or inquiry and to use a red flashing light to stop such vehicles.

headings.title: Livestock seizure, citations, civil penalties, and appeals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Covers 48-hour initial seizure and impoundment for suspected transport violations, state veterinarian or deputy determination invoking section 267.531 notice, redemption, expenses, hearing, and sale procedures, citations and summonses, civil penalties up to $10,000 after a section 276.631 hearing, and circuit court appeals under chapter 621 in the person's county of residence or Cole County. Independent review revised title to cover chapter 621 circuit-court appeals and specify civil penalties in contrast with subsection 1 misdemeanor penalties.

headings.title: Assistance from local and state law enforcement officials
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and source notes. Distinguishes permissive assistance ('may assist') by county and municipal law enforcement officials from mandatory assistance ('shall assist') by state law enforcement officials upon request within their respective jurisdictional powers.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections and history/prior-revision notes (RSMo 1939 § 14217 through A.L. 1987 H.B. 368; 1929–1909); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked sections 267.010–267.730, 267.531, 276.631, and chapter 621 cross-references, 48-hour initial impoundment, $10,000 civil penalty, and permissive local vs. mandatory state law-enforcement assistance. Retained subsections 1–3 and 5; revised subsection 4 to cover chapter 621 appeals and specify civil penalties.

headings.title: Governor-ordered out-of-state disease investigations and reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 14206, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1816; prior revisions 1929–1909; effective 5-10-78). Covers the governor's discretionary order directing the state veterinarian to investigate reported dangerous or infectious diseases in another state or territory and submit findings and suggestions.

headings.title: Formulating interstate and foreign livestock transport rules
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Covers the governor convening the director of agriculture and state veterinarian upon official report to arrange livestock transport rules into or through Missouri from diseased states, territories, or foreign countries if deemed wise.

headings.title: Gubernatorial quarantine proclamations and import restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Requires the governor, upon approving the rules, to issue a proclamation scheduling and quarantining affected localities and prohibiting importation and unloading of capable livestock except under those rules. Independent review revised "importation bans" to "import restrictions" to avoid presenting rule-qualified restrictions ("except under the aforesaid rules and regulations") as an unconditional ban.

headings.title: Carrier notice, penalties, damages, health-certificate exception, and venue
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and source notes. Covers sending approved rules to livestock carriers, misdemeanor fines ($1,000 to $10,000 per offense) and civil damages for prohibited transport, the damages immunity proviso for stock shipped with proper inspection and a health certificate, and circuit court penalty recovery in any county into or through which stock is brought.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 14206, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1816; 1929–1909; effective 5-10-78); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked discretionary investigation and rulemaking language, rule-qualified import restrictions, $1,000–$10,000 carrier fines, health-certificate damages proviso, and circuit-court venue. Retained subsections 1, 2, and 4; revised subsection 3 from "importation bans" to "import restrictions" to preserve the rule exception.

headings.title: Intrastate quarantine rules and gubernatorial movement proclamations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 14207, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1816; prior revisions 1929–1909; effective 5-10-78). Covers convening the director of agriculture and state veterinarian when disease is epidemic or found in Missouri municipalities, districts, or herds to formulate movement rules, followed by gubernatorial approval and a quarantine proclamation barring movement except under those rules.

headings.title: County commission notice, compliance, and sheriff assistance orders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Requires notifying the county commission (or legally substituted court) of the quarantined locality with copies of regulations, compliance by the commission, and issuing an order directing the sheriff to assist the state veterinarian.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 14207, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1816; 1929–1909; effective 5-10-78); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked intrastate scope distinguishing this section from 267.240, county commission or legally substituted court notice, and sheriff assistance orders. Retained both headings.

headings.title: Premises entry for cattle inspection and tuberculin testing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 14225, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1816; prior revision 1929 § 12545; effective 5-10-78). Authorizes the state veterinarian and authorized inspectors to enter barns, yards, pastures, buildings, or enclosures where cattle are kept to inspect and apply tuberculin tests under sections 267.010 to 267.460 conforming to USDA uniform methods and rules.

headings.title: Owner or custodian authority to confine animals for testing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source notes. Grants owners or custodians of domestic animals ordered inspected, examined, or tested by the state veterinarian the right and authority to confine and restrain them as directed. Independent review revised title to include custodians as well as owners ("Any owner or custodian of any domestic animal or animals").

headings.title: Refusal certification and sheriff duty to confine animals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Directs the state veterinarian, deputy, or assistants to certify an owner's or custodian's failure to confine or restrain animals to the county sheriff, who must forthwith cause the animals to be confined or restrained for testing or examination.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history/effective-date notes (RSMo 1939 § 14225, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1816; 1929 § 12545; effective 5-10-78); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked cattle-specific tuberculin entry under 267.010–267.460 and USDA uniform methods vs. broader domestic-animal confinement by owners or custodians and sheriff certification. Retained subsections 1 and 3; revised subsection 2 to include custodians.

headings.title: Entry and transit restrictions for diseased or quarantined animals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 3). Prohibits shipping or moving diseased, recently exposed, or quarantine-origin livestock or animals into or through Missouri without prior written permission from the state veterinarian, except diseased animals approved for restricted interstate shipment by the USDA Animal Disease Eradication Division. Independent review revised title to cover movement both "into or through the state" rather than entry alone.

headings.title: Health certificate or permit requirement and market exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires an accompanying official health certificate and/or permit for incoming livestock (attached to waybill or with driver/custodian), qualified by exceptions under sections 267.560 to 267.660, department rules, and consignments to supervised public stockyards or licensed markets with waybill, bill of lading, or ownership documentation unless required by the state veterinarian.

headings.title: Origin-state approval and transmittal of health certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires immediately forwarding a copy of the official health certificate to the origin state's livestock sanitary official for approval and transmittal to the Missouri state veterinarian, and mandates origin-state official approval on all health certificates.

headings.title: Quarantine at owner expense for undocumented livestock
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Directs that livestock or herds entering Missouri without a required health certificate or permit be quarantined at the owner's risk and expense for observation, testing, vaccination, dipping, treatment, and reinspection until released by the department.

headings.title: Obtaining livestock exhibition requirements from state veterinarian
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Directs that requirements for exhibiting livestock or herds be secured by contacting the Missouri state veterinarian.

headings.title: Release requirements for stockyard and unknown-origin animals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires animals covered under sections 267.560 to 267.660 originating from Missouri public stockyards or licensed markets, or assembled at markets or concentration points from unknown origins, to satisfy Missouri department regulations or destination-state laws and regulations prior to release.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 3); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked entry and transit scope, USDA restricted-shipment and supervised-market exceptions, origin-state approval, owner-expense quarantine, exhibition inquiry, and stockyard/unknown-origin release rules under 267.560–267.660. Retained subsections 2–6; revised subsection 1 to include transit ("into or through the state").

headings.title: Health certificate contents, thirty-day expiration, and department validation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 4). Specifies required consignor, consignee, origin, destination, description, health-status, test, and vaccination information for health certificates under sections 267.560 to 267.660, 30-day voiding after inspection and issuance, full-compliance validity, and the exception allowing written department validation of noncompliant certificates.

headings.title: Veterinarians authorized to inspect incoming livestock
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes accredited, licensed, graduate veterinarians approved or employed by the origin state's livestock sanitary official and USDA Animal Disease Eradication Division veterinarians to inspect livestock entering Missouri.

headings.title: Approved laboratories for pre-entry diagnostic tests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires pre-entry diagnostic tests for Missouri-bound animals to be conducted in state or federal laboratories, origin-state-approved laboratories, or USDA-supervised commercial laboratories approved by the origin state.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 4); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked required health-certificate contents, 30-day voiding, written department validation exception for noncompliant certificates, authorized origin/USDA veterinarians, and approved pre-entry diagnostic laboratories. Retained all three headings.

headings.title: Required information in entry permit requests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 5). Directs entry permit requests to the state veterinarian and enumerates required consignor, consignee, animal count/kind, origin, dates, destination, purpose, and transport method details.

headings.title: Missouri consignee requirement for permitted animals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires animals entering Missouri under permit to be consigned to a Missouri resident individual or a legal entity authorized by law to do business in the state.

headings.title: Fifteen-day permit expiration and shorter designated periods
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Provides that entry permits are void 15 days after issuance or after a shorter period designated by the state veterinarian.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 5); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked permit-request fields, Missouri resident or authorized-business consignee requirement, and 15-day or shorter state-veterinarian-designated voiding period. Retained all three headings.

headings.title: Carrier compliance with sections 267.560 to 267.660
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 6). Prohibits owners and operators of railroads, trucks, airplanes, and other conveyances from moving livestock, animals, or birds into, through, or within Missouri except in compliance with sections 267.560 to 267.660 and adopted department rules.

headings.title: General sanitation requirement for livestock conveyances
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires railway cars, trucks, airplanes, and other conveyances used to transport livestock and birds to be maintained in a clean, sanitary condition.

headings.title: Supervised disinfection after carrying diseased or exposed animals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Distinguished from subsection 2 by requiring conveyances that carried infected or exposed livestock, animals, or birds to be thoroughly cleaned and disinfected under official supervision before reuse for livestock transportation. Independent review revised title to preserve applicability to conveyances carrying exposed as well as infected animals.

headings.title: Carrier verification of shipment preparation and health documents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires conveyance owners and operators to ensure consignments are prepared under sections 267.560 to 267.660 and accompanied by an official health certificate or permit attached to the waybill or held by the attendant.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 6); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked carrier compliance under 267.560–267.660, general conveyance sanitation vs. supervised disinfection after carrying infected or exposed animals, and shipment-preparation/document checks. Retained subsections 1, 2, and 4; revised subsection 3 to include exposed animals.

headings.title: Grounds and procedure for governor-approved area quarantines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 (including subdivisions (1)–(5) and the closing continuation clause in block 11) and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 8). Lists five essential grounds for area quarantine under sections 267.560 to 267.660, notice from the state veterinarian to the director, governor-approved quarantine order by the director or state veterinarian, and inclusion of owner terms and conditions.

headings.title: Newspaper and radio notice of area quarantines
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires publicizing area quarantine orders against animal or bird movement in newspapers and on radios serving the affected area.

headings.title: Designation and prohibition of immunizing agents and tests
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes the department to designate immunizing agents or tests for disease control and eradication and to prohibit anyone from using agents the state veterinarian judges ineffective or non-expeditious.

headings.title: Restrictions or embargoes on unquarantined out-of-state areas
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Authorizes the director of agriculture, upon notice from the state veterinarian, to impose movement restrictions or a full embargo on livestock from an out-of-state area favoring disease introduction into Missouri where that state's officials have not quarantined or controlled movement.

headings.title: When out-of-state restriction or embargo orders take effect
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Makes an out-of-state restriction or complete embargo order effective upon notice in writing or by telegram to the affected state's livestock sanitary official. Independent review revised title to remove ambiguity in "Effective notice" and state directly that written or telegram notice triggers effectiveness.

headings.title: Required cooperation by licensed stockyards, markets, and dealers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Requires licensed Missouri public stockyards, other markets, traders, and dealers to cooperate with the department during in-state area quarantines or out-of-state livestock entry restrictions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all six subsections, subdivisions (1)–(5) and closing continuation clause of subsection 1, and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 8); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked governor-approved area quarantine grounds, newspaper/radio publicity, immunizing-agent controls, out-of-state restrictions/embargoes and written/telegram effective notice, and licensed-market/dealer cooperation. Retained subsections 1–4 and 6; revised subsection 5 to clarify when out-of-state orders take effect.

headings.title: Removal limits during testing or investigation and eradication discretion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/footnote notes (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 9, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1662). Bars removing animals, livestock, or birds under contagious/infectious disease test or investigation until specified disease-free certification, slaughter-on-permit, recovery, or official release conditions occur, and places eradication methods at the state veterinarian's discretion.

headings.title: Premises holding period during disease investigation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and source footnote. Authorizes the state veterinarian or representative to implement a holding period for premises* until disease investigation and confirmation finish; retains the Revisor's footnote discrepancy noting that the word 'premise' appears in the original rolls. Independent review removed "Temporary" to adhere strictly to statutory wording ("holding period for the premises* until the investigation and confirmation ... is completed"); original-rolls footnote ("premise") verified.

headings.title: Release or permanent quarantine after investigation and testing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Directs that once investigation and testing are complete, animals or birds must either be released from the holding period or placed under permanent quarantine by the state veterinarian or representative.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections, history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 9, A.L. 2010 H.B. 1662), and Revisor footnote (*Word "premise" appears in original rolls vs. "premises*" in subsection 2); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked conditional removal limits, eradication discretion, holding period until investigation and confirmation finish, and subsequent release or permanent quarantine. Retained subsections 1 and 3; revised subsection 2 to drop added word "Temporary" and preserve exact statutory phrasing and footnote discrepancy.

headings.title: Testing and disposition orders for quarantined livestock
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/effective-date notes (L. 1989 S.B. 300; effective 5-04-89). Authorizes the state veterinarian to require scheduled testing or retesting of quarantined livestock and requires owners to comply with removal, disposition, or cure orders if disease is discovered. Independent review removed "Required" to preserve the discretionary testing order language ("may be required by the state veterinarian") alongside mandatory compliance with disposition orders.

headings.title: Violation hearings, subpoena powers, civil penalties, and dismissal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 (including subdivisions (1) and (2)) and source notes. Covers county violation hearings summoned within 20 days, party presentation rights, subpoena/deposition/fee/mileage/oath powers of the director or representative, and post-hearing discretion to assess civil penalties (up to $1,000 per violation and up to $500 per day of noncompliance) or dismiss the case.

headings.title: Trial de novo appeals and penalty fund crediting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and source notes. Grants aggrieved persons an appeal to circuit court for a trial de novo in the county of quarantine and credits all assessed penalties to the Livestock Dealer Law Enforcement and Administration Fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections, subdivisions (1)–(2) of subsection 2, and history/effective-date notes (L. 1989 S.B. 300; effective 5-04-89); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked discretionary testing/retesting orders vs. mandatory compliance with disease-disposition orders, 20-day county hearing and subpoena/civil-penalty/dismissal powers, and circuit-court trial de novo plus Livestock Dealer Law Enforcement and Administration Fund crediting. Retained subsections 2–3; revised subsection 1 to remove unconditional "Required".

headings.title: Laboratory reporting of contagious disease findings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 10). Requires all laboratories, private or otherwise, to report findings of contagious, communicable, or infectious disease in submitted specimens as required by the department. Independent review removed "Mandatory" for neutrality and to avoid flattening the "and as may be required by the department" qualification.

headings.title: Department permit requirement for animal diagnostic laboratories
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires laboratory operators to apply for and obtain a department permit to conduct diagnostic tests on animals, birds, or tissues; retains the archived source wording 'as may be submitted by such laboratories' without silently altering it.

headings.title: Laboratory permit qualification, suspension, and revocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires the department to determine laboratory qualification before issuing a permit and provides for suspending or revoking a permit at any time for noncompliance with sections 267.560 to 267.660 and department rules.

headings.title: Live or virulent hog cholera virus prohibition and exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Prohibits use of live or virulent hog cholera virus effective on and after January 1, 1960, subject to exceptions provided in department rules. Independent review narrowed title to "live or virulent hog cholera virus" to match statutory scope; historical January 1, 1960 effective date verified without asserting current enforceability.

headings.title: Disease reporting duty for livestock owners and veterinarians
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Makes it unlawful for livestock or animal owners under sections 267.560 to 267.660 or veterinarians to withhold knowledge of or fail to report contagious or communicable diseases.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all five subsections and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 10); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked department-qualified laboratory reporting, archived phrasing "as may be submitted by such laboratories" in subsection 2 (retained faithfully), permit qualification/suspension/revocation under 267.560–267.660, historical January 1, 1960 prohibition on live or virulent hog cholera virus with rule exception, and owner/veterinarian reporting. Retained subsections 2, 3, and 5; revised subsection 1 for neutrality and subsection 4 to preserve "live or virulent" scope.

headings.title: Disease-control slaughter, indemnification limits, and food-use exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 310). Covers slaughter triggered when the state veterinarian judges it the sole eradication means or when USDA cooperative agreements require it, owner notice, appropriation-limited indemnification at the director's rate (capped at $800 for ostriches and emu), supervised destruction, and discretionary permitted slaughter for food under federal or approved municipal meat inspection.

headings.title: Accounting and payment of slaughter and disinfection costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires a department or USDA representative to keep a careful account of killing, burying, cleaning, and disinfection costs, paid by the state upon director approval.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1999 S.B. 310); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked slaughter triggers, appropriation-limited indemnification with the $800 ostrich/emu cap, discretionary food-use slaughter permit exception under federal or approved municipal meat inspection, and director-approved state payment of killing, burying, cleaning, and disinfection costs. Retained both headings.

headings.title: License for leasing male bovine or suis breeding animals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 12). Prohibits persons, firms, partnerships, corporations, or associations from leasing, loaning, or renting male bovine or suis breeding animals for compensation without first obtaining a department license. Independent review revised title to make "breeding animals" explicit as the statutory scope of the licensing rule.

headings.title: Required license application contents and business address
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires applicants to state the nature of the business, full local and post-office address, and any additional information required by the department.

headings.title: Annual per-animal license fees, renewal, and fund deposit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Sets annual license fees at $15 per male bovine and $5 per male suis (retaining source phrasing 'each of every male animal of the suis species'), January 1 annual renewal, and deposit of collected fees to the veterinary fees fund.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 12); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked breeding-animal leasing/loaning/renting license for male bovine or suis species, application contents, $15/$5 annual fees (faithfully noting source wording "each of every male animal of the suis species"), January 1 renewal, and veterinary fees fund deposit. Retained subsections 2–3; revised subsection 1 to specify breeding animals.

headings.title: License requirement for bovine or suis semen production
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 13). Prohibits engaging in the business of producing semen for artificial insemination of female bovine or suis animals without first obtaining a department license.

headings.title: Annual per-animal license fees and January 1 renewal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Sets annual license fees at $15 per male bovine and $5 per male suis with January 1 annual renewal; unlike section 267.615(3), this subsection does not include a veterinary-fees-fund deposit clause.

headings.title: Department health standards for semen-producing male animals
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires male bovine or suis animals used to produce semen for artificial insemination to meet health standards established by department rules and regulations.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 13); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked bovine/suis semen-production license, $15/$5 annual fees and January 1 renewal (noting absence of a fund-deposit clause unlike 267.615(3)), and department health standards for semen-producing males. Retained all three headings.

headings.title: Application and conditions for herd or flock certification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 17). Covers permissive state veterinarian certification of a herd or flock as free of a specific disease upon owner application, agreement to follow a control/eradication plan, passing tests, and satisfying department and USDA requirements.

headings.title: Issuance and duration of jointly approved certificates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires the department to issue a certificate approved by both the department and the USDA for the rule-prescribed duration once the owner has fully complied with certification requirements.

headings.title: Removal or cancellation of certification for rule violations
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Authorizes the state veterinarian to remove or cancel disease-free certification when a herd or flock owner violates status-maintenance rules.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 17); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked permissive state veterinarian certification upon owner application/compliance with department and USDA standards, jointly approved certificate issuance and duration, and cancellation for rule violations. Retained all three headings.

headings.title: USDA cooperation and premises entry under sections 267.560 to 267.660
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 18, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52). Authorizes and directs the Department of Agriculture to cooperate with the USDA under sections 267.560 to 267.660 and empowers entry at any time into premises, barns, stables, sheds, vehicles, or other places where livestock or birds are kept for administration and enforcement. Independent review specified "premises entry" to avoid confusion with livestock "entry" into the state in subsection 2.

headings.title: Rulemaking authority under section 267.122 and chapter 536
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Authorizes the department to adopt rules pursuant to section 267.122 and chapter 536 to enforce sections 267.560 to 267.660, including rules governing entry and movement of livestock, animals, or birds into, within, and through Missouri.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1959 H.B. 501 § 18, A.L. 1993 S.B. 52); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked USDA cooperation, premises/vehicle inspection entry under 267.560–267.660, and rulemaking under 267.122 and chapter 536 for livestock entry and movement. Retained subsection 2; revised subsection 1 to specify "premises entry" to distinguish it from livestock entry in subsection 2.

headings.title: Approved dipping facilities and required consignment records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 26 § 4). Requires sheep and goat market operators and dealers to provide department-approved dipping facilities and maintain detailed origin, receipt, dipping, and consignment document records for incoming and outgoing shipments.

headings.title: One-year retention and inspection of incoming documents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires retaining incoming waybills, permits, and health or inspection certificates for one year and making them available on demand to a department or division representative.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1961 p. 26 § 4); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked approved dipping facilities and detailed consignment records for sheep and goat market operators and dealers, and one-year retention/demand inspection of incoming documents. Retained both headings.

headings.title: Supervised dipping requirement for breeding or feeding movement
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/footnote notes (L. 1961 p. 26 § 13). Bars sheep or goats from Missouri counties or areas not certified scabies-free from entering scabies-free areas for breeding or feeding unless dipped in an approved dip under supervision within 10 days before movement with dipping evidence accompanying the shipment and provided to the purchaser or consignee.

headings.title: Market-consignment exception for undipped sheep and goats
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and Revisor footnote. Allows undipped sheep and goats from noncertified areas not known to be infected* with or exposed to scabies to enter certified scabies-free areas only when consigned directly to a stockyards or licensed auction market with specified shipping or inspection documents; retains the footnote noting the word 'affected' appears in the original rolls.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections, history note (L. 1961 p. 26 § 13), and Revisor footnote (*Word "affected" in original rolls vs. "infected*" in subsection 2); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked 10-day supervised dipping rule for breeding/feeding movement from noncertified to scabies-free Missouri areas and the direct stockyards/licensed-auction consignment exception with required documents. Retained both headings and original-rolls caveat.

headings.title: Health certificates, stockyard exception, and feeding-animal permits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 26 § 16). Requires origin health certificates showing disease-free status and certified scabies-free origin for imported breeding or feeding sheep and goats, with a qualified exception for full-time federal stockyards inspection consignments carrying waybill identification for registered breeding animals, plus a Missouri state veterinarian permit requirement for feeding sheep and goats.

headings.title: Non-scabies-free origin dipping, special permits, and slaughter imports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers 10-day supervised dipping certificates for breeding or feeding sheep and goats from non-scabies-free states or areas (with a special-permit exception where not barred by federal interstate rules) and clinical inspection certificates plus 72-hour post-entry slaughter for slaughter sheep and goats from non-scabies-free origins.

headings.title: One-year market and dealer retention of incoming documents
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires markets and dealers to retain incoming waybills, permits, and health or inspection certificates for one year and make them available at all times upon demand to department or division representatives.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections and history note (L. 1961 p. 26 § 16); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked origin health certificates, full-time federal stockyards inspection exception with registered-animal waybills, feeding-animal permits, non-scabies-free 10-day dipping/special-permit/72-hour slaughter import rules, and one-year market/dealer document retention. Retained all three headings.

headings.title: Shearer registration, annual renewal, and own-flock exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 26 § 14). Requires sheep or goat shearers to register with the department within 30 days (retaining the 1961 unanchored statutory timing text) and annually on January 1, and prohibits unregistered persons from shearing sheep or goats other than their own.

headings.title: Equipment cleaning and disinfection in scabies counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Requires shearers operating in department-determined scabies counties to clean and disinfect equipment immediately after each shearing operation and before leaving the premises following department procedures.

headings.title: Five-day reporting of suspected or evident scabies
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Requires sheep or goat shearers to report any suspicion or evidence of scabies within five days to the state, district, or area veterinarian or area livestock inspector with owner and premises location details.

headings.title: Shearing recordkeeping and one-year retention for inspection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Requires shearers to keep records of animal counts, owner names and addresses, and shearing dates for one year and make them available on demand to a department or division representative.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history note (L. 1961 p. 26 § 14); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked unanchored 1961 30-day registration wording, annual January 1 renewal, own-flock shearing exception, equipment disinfection in scabies counties, five-day scabies reporting, and one-year shearing recordkeeping. Retained all four headings.

headings.title: Initial and annual January 1 dealer registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1961 p. 26 § 15). Requires dealers to register with the department on department forms within 30 days (retaining the 1961 unanchored statutory timing text) and annually on January 1 thereafter.

headings.title: Regular inspection of dealers' premises
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Directs that dealers' premises be inspected at regular intervals by a department or division representative.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1961 p. 26 § 15); verified all source and subsection fingerprints. Checked unanchored 1961 30-day initial dealer registration wording, annual January 1 registration, and regular premises inspection by department or division representatives. Retained both headings.
